fields.rationale: Neither AHB IHI 0033C nor APB IHI 0024C defines a JTAG / scan / BIST / MBIST / debug architecture. There is no dedicated debug interface in either protocol. Debug visibility, if any, must be added by the integrator outside these specs (e.g. via ARM CoreSight components on the SoC).

spec_provided_observability_ahb.name: HRESP error response
spec_provided_observability_ahb.purpose: Subordinate's two-cycle ERROR response is observable by the Manager and any monitoring logic.

spec_provided_observability_ahb.name: HEXOKAY (AHB5)
spec_provided_observability_ahb.purpose: Indicates success or failure of an Exclusive Transfer; can be used to detect contention in Exclusive sequences.

spec_provided_observability_ahb.name: User signaling AxUSER (AHB5)
spec_provided_observability_ahb.purpose: Optional User-defined signals on each channel (HAUSER / HWUSER / HRUSER / HBUSER) — implementation-defined extras for debug / trace / functional augmentation; spec recommends only point-to-point use due to interoperability risk.

spec_provided_observability_ahb.name: Interface protection using parity (AHB5)
spec_provided_observability_ahb.purpose: Optional byte-parity signals (HADDRCHK, HCTRLCHK, HWDATACHK, HRDATACHK, HRESPCHK, HREADYCHK) and a per-interface error indicator — allows detection of single-bit faults on each interface.

spec_provided_observability_ahb.name: Default Subordinate DECERR-equivalent
spec_provided_observability_ahb.purpose: Decoder routes unsupported addresses to a default Subordinate that issues an ERROR response for NONSEQ/SEQ (and zero-wait OKAY for IDLE/BUSY).

spec_provided_observability_apb.name: PSLVERR (APB3+)
spec_provided_observability_apb.purpose: Subordinate may signal failure of a transfer in the last cycle; PSLVERR mapped back to HRESP=ERROR / RRESP=SLVERR by an upstream bridge.

ahb_optional_features_per_property.Write_Strobes: Adds HWSTRB to the interface for sparse-write support
ahb_optional_features_per_property.Secure_Transfers: Adds HNONSEC; supports Secure/Non-secure transfer distinction
ahb_optional_features_per_property.Exclusive_Transfers: Adds HEXCL + HMASTER + HEXOKAY; supports Exclusive Access Monitor
ahb_optional_features_per_property.Extended_Memory_Types: Widens HPROT to 7 bits (HPROT[6:0]) for extended memory-type encoding
ahb_optional_features_per_property.User_Request_Width: HAUSER user signal width on the address channel (issuer-defined)
ahb_optional_features_per_property.User_Data_Width: HWUSER / HRUSER user signal widths on the data channels
ahb_optional_features_per_property.User_Response_Width: HBUSER user signal width on the response channel
ahb_optional_features_per_property.Parity_Property: Enables interface protection using parity check signals

fields.ahb_recommendations_on_user_signals: Spec recommends against general use of HxUSER signals on an interconnect because their semantics are not standardized — interoperability risk. They are intended for point-to-point Manager-Subordinate communication only.

evidence.quote: AHB defines optional user-defined signals on each channel. The widths are interface properties (USER_REQ_WIDTH, USER_DATA_WIDTH, USER_RESP_WIDTH). The User signals are not propagated through generic interconnect components.

Parity check signals can be used to provide interface protection. HADDRCHK protects HADDR; HCTRLCHK protects control bits; HWDATACHK protects HWDATA; HRDATACHK protects HRDATA; HRESPCHK protects HRESP; HREADYCHK protects HREADY. Single-bit error detection capability.
ERROR response is a two-cycle response on HRESP.

If a system design does not contain a completely filled memory map, then an additional default Subordinate must be implemented to provide a response when any of the nonexistent address locations are accessed. If a NONSEQUENTIAL or SEQUENTIAL transfer is attempted to a nonexistent address location, then the default Subordinate provides an ERROR response. IDLE or BUSY transfers to nonexistent locations result in a zero wait state OKAY response.
You can use PSLVERR to indicate an error condition on an APB transfer. APB peripherals are not required to support the PSLVERR pin.
